track.title: Chemistry
track.summary: A conceptual and quantitative path for understanding matter, atoms, compounds, and reactions.

orientationEssays.title: What is Chemistry?
orientationEssays.plainLanguageSummary: Chemistry is the study of what things are made of and how they change. It helps you see matter as patterns of particles and transformations.
orientationEssays.historicalOrigin: Chemistry began in older practices such as fire, cooking, dyes, metals, medicines, fermentation, glass, and pottery. Measurement later transformed recipes into modern science.
orientationEssays.socialImportance: Chemistry sits underneath food, medicine, climate, energy, batteries, materials, agriculture, and pollution. It affects what societies can make and repair.
orientationEssays.whyLearnersCare: Chemistry gives everyday changes a deeper explanation: bread rising, iron rusting, fuel burning, medicine dissolving, or batteries powering a phone.
commonObjections: Learners may think formulas are arbitrary symbols disconnected from visible reality.
Learners may expect atoms to disappear during reactions instead of rearranging.
deeperPaths: Study atomic structure and bonding to understand why reactions happen.
Connect conservation of mass to stoichiometry and laboratory measurement.
sourceNotes: Seeded from the project plan orientation requirements and introductory chemistry scope.

concepts.title: Conservation of Mass in Reactions
concepts.summary: Chemical reactions rearrange atoms; they do not create or destroy atoms.
objectives: Explain why both sides of a chemical equation must contain the same number of each atom.

hints: Start with nitrogen, then adjust hydrogen.

feedback.correct: Correct. Both sides have 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms.
feedback.incorrect: Count each atom on both sides. The same element must have the same total count.

evidenceRequired: Balances an equation by preserving atom counts.

hints: There are two hydrogen atoms and two chlorine atoms on the left.

feedback.correct: Correct. The coefficient 2 in front of HCl balances both atoms.
feedback.incorrect: Count hydrogen and chlorine separately on each side.

misconceptions.description: Learner treats a chemical reaction as if atoms can vanish instead of rearranging.

remediation.message: Represent atoms as tokens and move them from reactants into products without losing any tokens.

concepts.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
concepts.summary: Use coefficients to make each element count match on both sides of a reaction.
objectives: Balance a chemical equation by changing coefficients, not subscripts.

hints: Balance carbon, then hydrogen, then oxygen.

feedback.correct: Correct. The equation has 1 C, 4 H, and 4 O atoms on each side.
feedback.incorrect: Check oxygen last after carbon and hydrogen are balanced.

evidenceRequired: Balances multi-element equations using coefficients only.

hints: Use an even number of oxygen atoms in Al2O3 products.

feedback.correct: Correct. Four aluminum atoms and six oxygen atoms appear on each side.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the formulas the same and change only coefficients.

misconceptions.description: Learner changes subscripts inside formulas instead of changing coefficients.

remediation.message: Practice keeping each compound formula fixed while only adding whole-number coefficients.
